comments.author: @GrahameMcLeod
comments.text: Great video. You point out that the Antarctica is a very harsh place and is hostile to humans.  And that there is a need to provide life support systems for survival. But all the life support is already there - we can breathe the air without suffocating, atmospheric pressure is 1 bar and so our body fluids do not boil away, no radiation from outer space, and gravity of 1 g thus ensuring that our bodies do not waste away. All we have to do is to modify the temperature. The place is far, far less hostile than Mars where scientists are already drawing up plans to build future cities of thousands of people on a planet that is infinitely more hostile than Antarctica. But there are no cities yet in Antarctica!

replies.author: @BestTravel2
replies.text: That's a fascinating perspective you've brought up, and a great point about the inherent life support systems already present on Earth, even in Antarctica. It certainly puts the challenges of Mars into a different light!
